solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Slippery item beginning to bother a relative's family

indicators.note: the beginning of 'bother' is its first letter

parts.note: nana is a grandmother; the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: Something slippery threatens to cause trouble for a relative's household.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive S runs straight into KIN, so the answer's word break falls inside a piece. Nana is an informal word for grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana skin is the classic thing to slip on, and figuratively a pitfall.

clue.text: Lady Godiva's attire represented a British duty

indicators.note: re-presented: the letters are presented again in a new order

explanation.surface: Lady Godiva's naked ride is framed as a patriotic obligation.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Godiva is the legendary noblewoman who rode naked through Coventry, so her 'attire' was none at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A birthday suit is bare skin, which is all Lady Godiva wore.

clue.text: Masked warrior partially hidden in Jakarta

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: A masked fighter lies half-concealed somewhere in Jakarta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hidden' looks like the instruction, but it is fodder: its last letter starts the answer, and 'partially' does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninjas were Japanese covert fighters, traditionally shown masked.

clue.text: Sister needed up north primarily

indicators.note: take the prime, or first, letter of each word

explanation.surface: A sister is required in the north of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a request for a nurse or nun somewhere up north; only 'primarily' says to read the three initials instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuns are addressed by the title Sister, so the definition names one by her form of address.

clue.text: Pacific islander as upset over complaint

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down, so they read backwards

explanation.surface: An islander is annoyed about some grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'over' also means on top of, so the upturned AS sits above MOAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Samoans come from Samoa, in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Position in prison for certain kind of crime?

explanation.surface: Someone asks what post a convict holds, and what crime it suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the reverse order of the clue: JOB is 'Position', written first, but it ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An inside job is a crime committed with help from someone within the organisation robbed.

clue.text: Aspire to change ancient empire

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to reform an old empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aspire' sits first as if it were the verb of the sentence, but it is only six letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Persia was the ancient empire centred on modern Iran.

clue.text: Dance is with editor to secure perfect location?

parts.note: a prom is a formal dance
to land a deal is to secure it

explanation.surface: A dance and an editor combine to book the ideal venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secure' reads as a verb acting on the location, but it is simply LAND. The question mark flags the definition as loose: a promised land is ideal, not literally perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: The promised land is a longed-for place of happiness, from the land promised to Abraham.

clue.text: Period of time immediately before altercation

definitions.meaning: the lead-up stretch before an event, as before an election
a quarrel or brush with someone, e.g. with the police

explanation.surface: The moments just before a fight broke out.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no wordplay here: the surface fuses the two meanings into one story of the minutes before a scuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Run-in covers both the approach to an event and an argument or confrontation.

clue.text: Assemble most of currency for rubber?

indicators.note: take all but the last letter

explanation.surface: Gathering nearly all your cash to buy an eraser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubber' looks like an eraser or a tyre; the question mark says it is one who rubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur rubs people's muscles for a living.

clue.text: Had learnt to move around central region

indicators.note: the letters move into new places

explanation.surface: Someone had learnt to travel about the middle of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a traveller's progress; 'to move around' is the instruction, and the fodder is the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A heartland is the central, most important part of a region.

clue.text: Money manager, initially tight, certain to cut back

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted money manager is determined to make cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: The commas make 'cut back' look like a spending cut; in fact 'cut' is the container instruction and 'back' is the word being cut into.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasurer is the title in clubs and companies for the officer who looks after the funds, a fair gloss as a money manager.

clue.text: Total is small? Let me think …

parts.note: S = small, as on clothing labels
um is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone pauses to decide whether a total is small.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis and question mark make it look like hesitant speech; 'Let me think …' is exactly that hesitation, written as UM.
explanation.definitionFit: Sum and total are plain noun synonyms: the result of adding numbers up.

clue.text: Disney princess returns outside one part of church

indicators.note: the name comes back, reading backwards
the reversed name goes outside the letter for one

explanation.surface: A Disney princess comes back to stand outside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: ELSA turned around is ASLE, and I slips in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The aisle is the passage between the pews of a church.

clue.text: Try hard with new rivets

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A worker makes an effort with fresh rivets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' passes for an ordinary adjective describing the rivets; it is one of the commonest anagram signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: striving is making a strenuous effort.

clue.text: Trousers belonging to Sibelius, perhaps?

definitions.note: the second definition is possessive: JEAN'S, whose apostrophe the grid drops

definitions.meaning: the Finnish composer's first name, made possessive; 'perhaps' says he is one example

explanation.surface: A pair of trousers that once belonged to the Finnish composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Sibelius's first name was Jean, so his things are JEAN'S. Sibelius is the surname solvers know, which hides the first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeans are trousers, and Jean's means owned by a Jean.

clue.text: Setter put into vehicle with a picture taker

indicators.note: to put something into a container places it inside, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: The setter climbs into a car with someone taking photos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' means the person who wrote the clue, so it gives ME, not a dog or a jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the device that takes photographs, described by what it does.

clue.text: Title of father shortened

indicators.note: a shortened word has been cut down, here by losing its final letter

parts.note: SIRE, a father, without its last letter

explanation.surface: A father's title has been abbreviated.
explanation.walkthrough: Sire is an old word for a father, still used of horses; drop its E.
explanation.definitionFit: The honorific used for a knight or baronet, and as a polite form of address.

clue.text: Celebrity committee is at sea, right?

parts.note: a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: A celebrity asks whether a committee is confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' looks like it means bewildered; with 'right' it becomes the definition, right as sailors say it.
explanation.definitionFit: Starboard is the right-hand side of a ship, facing forward.

clue.text: Car with zero sound

parts.note: Audi is a make of car

explanation.surface: A car that makes no noise at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Car' is a make, not the general word, and the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a noun for sound, especially recorded or broadcast sound, as in a film's soundtrack.

clue.text: Opposite of fashionable poetry

explanation.surface: Something is the opposite of trendy poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opposite of' reads as one phrase; 'of' is only a link, and 'Opposite' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun synonym from logic and maths: reversing a relation gives its counterpart, as with the reciprocal of a fraction.

clue.text: Foolhardy hero holding back monster

indicators.note: the words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A reckless hero keeps a monster at bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding back' reads as restraining the monster; it is two instructions, hide and reverse. ARDYH read backwards is HYDRA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hydra was the many-headed monster killed by Hercules.

clue.text: Owns shears regularly

parts.note: sHeArS: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Someone possesses shears that they use routinely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' passes for an adverb about using the shears, but it says to take every other letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: to possess something, in the present tense to match 'Owns'.

clue.text: Dad borrows terribly big chopper

explanation.surface: Father helps himself to a huge axe without asking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopper' suggests an axe or a helicopter; here it is a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadsword is a large, broad-bladed sword for cutting blows.
